hero_kpi_rationale: The Midstream segment delivers stable growth with $2.8 B in revenue in 2025 (+7% YoY) and represents the strategic core of value creation for Phillips 66.

kpis.name: Net Income attributable to Phillips 66
kpis.explanation: Net income attributable to company shareholders
kpis.description: Net income of $4,403 million in 2025 reflects higher refining margins, gains from asset disposals, and strong Marketing segment performance.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures and Investments
kpis.description: The $2.2 billion investments in 2025 primarily fund the development of the Midstream segment, including $1.3 billion allocated to growth in 2026

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: The target of $17 Bn in total debt by end-2027 reflects management's priority on financial flexibility and cash generation.

kpis.name: Midstream Income Before Taxes
kpis.explanation: Pretax result of the Midstream segment (transportation, NGL, fractionation) reflecting the performance of energy infrastructure.
kpis.description: The Midstream segment generates $2,817 M in 2025, driven by NGL growth (+$553 M) offsetting Transport decline (-$374 M). Stable contribution over 3 years.

kpis.name: Marketing & Specialties Income Before Taxes
kpis.explanation: Pretax result of the Marketing & Specialties segment, including gains from asset disposals (Coop, Germany/Austria).
kpis.description: The segment surged to $4,500 M in 2025, benefiting from a $1.9 B gain on the partial sale of Germany/Austria operations and $1 B from the disposal of Coop. Excluding divestitures, the underlying operating base is more modest.

kpis.name: NGL Fractionated Volumes
kpis.explanation: Daily volume of fractionated natural gas liquids (NGL), a key indicator of Midstream processing activity, in thousands of barrels per day.
kpis.description: NGL fractionation reaches 896 Mbbl/d in 2025 versus 728 in 2024, driven by the Coastal Bend acquisition (April 2025) and increased Permian activity. Upward trend over 3 years.

kpis.name: Refining Income Before Taxes
kpis.explanation: Segment operating income for Refining, highly sensitive to crack margins and refined petroleum product prices.
kpis.description: Refining reports a loss of $274M in 2025, an improvement from -$365M in 2024, driven by stronger crack margins. This contrasts sharply with the $5,340M in 2023, illustrating the sector's cyclicality.

kpis.name: NGL Pipeline Throughput Y-Grade to Market
kpis.explanation: Gross NGL volume (Y-Grade) transported to fractionation hubs (Mont Belvieu, Sweeny, Conway), in thousands of barrels per day.
kpis.description: NGL throughput to market increases to 917 Mbbl/d in 2025 (+21.6%), reflecting the integration of Coastal Bend and ramp-up of Permian activities. Continued growth over 3 years.

kpis.name: EBITDA Ajusté Refining
kpis.explanation: Measures Phillips 66's refining segment profitability after adjustments, showing its ability to generate operational profits.

kpis.name: EBITDA Ajusté Midstream
kpis.explanation: Measures Phillips 66's midstream pipeline operations profitability, excluding one-time exceptional items.

kpis.name: EBITDA Marketing & Specialties
kpis.explanation: Measures operating profits of Marketing & Specialties division before interest, taxes, and depreciation.

kpis.name: Flux de Trésorerie Disponible
kpis.explanation: Measures actual cash Phillips 66 generates after expenses, showing ability to pay dividends and fund investments.

kpis.name: Utilisation Capacité Raffinage
kpis.explanation: Percentage of Phillips 66's refining capacity used to convert crude oil into fuels and petroleum products.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Dividend Per Share — total dividends paid divided by shares outstanding.
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend cut risk, monitor payout sustainability

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.explanation: Capital Return — total cash returned to shareholders (dividends + buybacks).
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Payout Ratio — dividends paid divided by net income.
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Dividend cut risk, monitor payout sustainability

stories_kpis.name: Midstream Revenue
stories_kpis.description: The Midstream segment generates $2.817 B in revenue in 2025, supported by integrated transportation and NGL activities, with strategic acquisitions including Coastal Bend and WRB
stories_kpis.signal: Stable growth in the Midstream segment

stories_kpis.name: Chemicals Revenue
stories_kpis.description: The Chemicals segment (50% JV with CPChem) generates $0.297 B in revenue in 2025, impacted by margin compression due to high ethane prices and industrial oversupply
stories_kpis.signal: Significant decline in Chemicals segment revenue.

ai_positioning.summary: The company Phillips 66 does not explicitly mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K report. The information provided focuses on the company's financial, operational, and transactional aspects.

risks.title: Fluctuations in oil prices
risks.summary: Fluctuations in oil and natural gas prices directly impact the profitability of the Refining, Midstream NGL and Chemicals segments.
risks.score_rationale: The energy sector is sensitive to fluctuations in oil and natural gas prices, which impact Phillips 66's profitability. Average WTI declined from $75.83/bbl in 2024 to $64.89/bbl in 2025. Refining margins (3:2:1 crack spread) have increased but are highly dependent on prices (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Environmental regulations
risks.summary: Stricter environmental and energy regulations impact operational strategies and compliance-related investments.
risks.score_rationale: Phillips 66 is subject to strict environmental regulations. The 10-K mentions the shutdown of fuel production at the Los Angeles refinery and the launch of renewable fuels activities, reflecting increasing regulatory pressure (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Energy industry competition
risks.summary: Competition in refining, midstream and distribution impacts margins and market share.
risks.score_rationale: The refining and energy distribution sector is highly competitive. Phillips 66 must maintain utilization rates above the industry average (94% in 2025) and a finished product yield > 86% to remain competitive (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Risques opérationnels
risks.summary: Operational risks associated with the production, transportation, and refining of oil may lead to disruptions and significant costs.
risks.score_rationale: Phillips 66 operates complex refineries and pipelines exposed to risks of disruptions, accidents, and maintenance. The shutdown of the Los Angeles refinery illustrates major operational risks that could impact cash flows (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Energy transition and oil demand
risks.summary: The global energy transition represents a major structural risk to traditional refining and petroleum product distribution activities.
risks.score_rationale: The transition to renewable energy and electrification is reducing long-term demand for oil and gas. Phillips 66 is diversifying through renewable fuels (Renewable Fuels segment), but structural risks remain significant (default score, to be refined).

governance.voting_structure_note: Single class of common stock, 1 vote per share.
